decisions.subject: Video topic

options_considered.label: OpenMontage product explainer
options_considered.reason: Useful but more promotional than craft-focused.

options_considered.label: Why the sky is blue (repo demo prompt)
options_considered.reason: Already documented in the repo's own README.

options_considered.label: How AI agents actually make a video
options_considered.reason: Lets the video demonstrate the exact pipeline it describes and is grounded in current, citable data.

decisions.selected: How AI agents actually make a video
decisions.reason: User delegated topic choice. This subject makes the film self-demonstrating and gives every claim a source.

decisions.subject: Visual style playbook

options_considered.label: Clean Professional (white, corporate)
options_considered.reason: Reads as generic corporate and flattens hierarchy.

options_considered.label: Flat Motion Graphics (dark, energetic)
options_considered.reason: Tuned for fast social pacing, which fights the narration.

options_considered.label: Premium Minimalist (off-white editorial, cobalt accent)
options_considered.reason: Calm authority, low ornament, restrained ease-out motion — matches a measured 62s expert explainer.

decisions.reason: Its documented taste profile matches the brief and keeps long text blocks legible without heavy scrims.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime

options_considered.label: Remotion (bundled default)
options_considered.reason: Browser download blocked; chrome-headless-shell host unreachable.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames (HTML/GSAP runtime)
options_considered.reason: puppeteer-core requires the same missing NSS libraries.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg runtime via video_compose
options_considered.reason: Requires no browser; video_compose supports it when the approved path explicitly names FFmpeg.

decisions.reason: Both bundled browser runtimes need a Chrome/Chromium build whose shared libraries (libnss3, libnspr4, libnssutil3) cannot be sourced in this environment. FFmpeg is the supported runtime for an approved FFmpeg path, so the swap is deliberate and disclosed rather than silent.

decisions.subject: Authoring mode

options_considered.label: Assembled from stock scene templates
options_considered.reason: Those templates render through the browser runtime, which is unavailable.

options_considered.label: Bespoke atelier composition
options_considered.reason: Gives frame-level authorship: pixel-exact typography, counters, diagrams and word-timed captions.

decisions.reason: With no browser runtime, frame-level authorship is the only route to real motion graphics — and it makes the typography exact.

decisions.subject: Narration TTS provider

options_considered.label: ElevenLabs (premium)
options_considered.reason: No API key; provider host unreachable.

options_considered.label: Google TTS (700+ voices)
options_considered.reason: No API key; provider host unreachable.

options_considered.label: Piper (free, offline)
options_considered.reason: Voice models download from a host outside the network allowlist.

options_considered.label: Platform TTS
options_considered.reason: Only reachable narration path; per-section synthesis locks the timeline to measured durations.

decisions.reason: Highest-quality narration available with no provider keys; section-level synthesis makes the edit timeline exact.

decisions.subject: Music bed

options_considered.label: Pixabay Music
options_considered.reason: Network blocked in this environment.

options_considered.label: Suno AI
options_considered.reason: No API key.

options_considered.label: Locally synthesised pad via FFmpeg
options_considered.reason: Royalty-free, reachable offline, level set from the playbook (0.07) with sidechain ducking.

decisions.reason: Keeps the mix legal and reproducible with no external service.

decisions.subject: Caption treatment

options_considered.label: Burned subtitles via libass
options_considered.reason: Would need an external transcript for word-level timings.

options_considered.label: Frame-level drawn captions
options_considered.reason: Timed by character-weighted distribution across each section's measured duration, so captions lock to narration without a transcription pass.

options_considered.label: No captions
options_considered.reason: Most social viewing is muted; captions are mandatory for reach.

decisions.reason: No transcriber is available, so captions are derived from the script's measured section durations — word-level accuracy without a transcription pass.

decisions.subject: Post-render QA corrections (v2)

options_considered.label: Ship the v1 render
options_considered.reason: Self-review had passed, but full-resolution QA then found a 2.35s closing-shot flash in every inter-scene gap and invisible scene-5 chip labels; both are visible defects.

options_considered.label: Fix and re-render
options_considered.reason: Four defects had clear, low-risk fixes; a re-render restores the delivery promise.

options_considered.label: Document without re-rendering
options_considered.reason: The defects are in the picture, not the paperwork.

decisions.reason: Frame scheduler now holds each scene through the 0.30-0.45s inter-scene gap and cross-fades into the next section start (the old fallback rendered the last scene, flashing the closing shot 7x for 2.35s); scene 5 layer-cache keys now include the card-state flag so chip labels are not baked in the pre-animation colour; scene 3's stat block clears the caption band; the progress rail reports film-wide progress. Review frames now sample scene midpoints - uniform eighths had landed inside a gap, which is why the v1 self-review missed the flashes.
